newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: PM CONFIDENT ABOUT ECONOMIC PROSPECTS
The prime Minister says the March quarter growth figures confirm consumer demand is picking up, the housing sector is strengthening and business investment remains very strong.
The March quarter figures show growth in the quarter at point nine per cent, and growth for the year at 2.4 per cent.
Mr Howard says there have been numerous reports in recent days of the potential strength of investment in the resource sector.
He says growth in 1997-98 is expected to be consistent with the budget estimate while growth in 1996-97 is likely to be three percent.
The Treasurer says growth in the June quarter will be more than one per ent and employment will improve by mid next year.
But Shadow Treasurer, Gareth Evans, says the Government's record is abysmal and Australians want action and results, not excuses.
COSTELLO SAYS CAR TARIFFS DECISION WILL BE BALANCED
The Federal Treasurer, Peter Costello, has promised the Government's decision on car industry tariffs will a sensible balance between competing factors.
A major report has recommended tariffs fall to five per cent by 2005, but the Opposition and car industry are arguing for tariffs to be frozen at around 15 per cent.
Mr Costello says the Government will come to a sensible balance on issues such as keeping a car industry and keeping to international targets on trade liberalisation.
But he warns nobody will get everything they want from the Government's decision.
EVANS NOT CONFIDENT ABOUT NATIVE TITLE MEETING WITH HOWARD
Deputy Opposition leader Gareth Evans says the ALP wants to lay the foundations for a continuing dialogue, in tonight's meeting with the Prime Minister on native title.
Mr Evans says the Opposition doesn't have any great optimism about quick returns from tonight's meeting.
But he says the Opposition isn't deterred by Mr Howard ruling out any change to the basic principles of his plan to deal with the High Court's Wik judgement.
Mr Evans says it'll be useful if there's a dialogue that bears fruit in several months, when the Senate and the House of Representatives may well be in a stand-off over the issue.
INSTITUTE OF SPORT DEFENDS AXING OF MILLER'S SCHOLARSHIP
The Head of the Australian Institute of Sport, John Boultbee, says taxpayers can't be expected to foot the bill for athletes who don't want to give 100-percent.
The AIS has revoked Scott Miller's scholarship, worth about 25,000 dollars a year, after he failed to attend training sessions at a swimming camp.
Mr Boultbee says he spoke to Miller about his lack of commitment last week, but his attitude didn't change.
Mr Boultbee says Miller is not the first and he won't be the last athlete who hasn't been able to meet the training commitment.
KENNETT DEFENDS USE OF GAMBLING REVENUE FOR ART PRIZE
Victorian Premier, Jeff Kennett has defended the Government's decision to use gambling revenue to fund a major contemporary art prize.
The 100,000 dollar prize was awarded to an Adelaide artist who made a room of cardboard boxes containing soap sculptures.

The Salvation Army says the Contempora Five prize money which comes from the Government Community Support Fund would have been better spent on helping people with gambling problems. But Mr Kennett says the arts have so far recieved $50 million from the Fund compared to $149 million spent on welfare.
He says the Salvation Army has already received $11.4 million.
HANSON DOLL HITS CYBERSPACE
One of the makers of a Pauline Hanson voodoo doll, being shown on the internet, says the idea is to prick the independent MP's conscience.
Cairns-based artist Michael Winer says the doll comes in a barbie doll-style box, is wrapped up in bandages and wax and includes pins, to prick Ms Hanson's conscience.
He says he's trying to make some more of the dolls before Ms Hanson visits Cairns in a few weeks, to get here thinking more deeply about the results of her actions and speeches.
Mr Winer and fellow artist Judith Taylor say there's keen demand for the dolls in San Francisco.
APPEAL BY TJANDA'S ATTACKER REJECTED
Queensland's Court of Appeal has dismissed an appeal by the man jailed for life for setting fire to a Cairns schoolboy last year.
In March, a Cairns jury found 27-year-old Paul Wade Streeton guilty of the attempted murder of six year old Tjandamurra O'Shane.
It found Streeton had doused Tjanmdamurra with petrol and set him alight in the grounds of a Cairns school in October last year.
Streeton told the Court of Appeal he never had an intent to kill Tjandamurra but his motivation was retribution against society.
He also said he had shown remorse.
But the Three court of appeal judges disagreed, refusing his appeal against conviction and refusing him leave to appeal against his sentence.
